answer: One credential opens exactly one identity: it derives one nullifier, recorded once, and reuse is rejected and slashed. A jetty berth admits one hull, so a second hull claiming it is turned away. Making 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 credentials at 50 credits each, 50,000 total; the k-th fake still costs a fresh credential, so marginal cost never falls. An honest agent pays 50 once and keeps a full reward share. The failure mode is credential rental: a rented credential passes a narrow inlet once, and old nullifiers stack like shale strata, exposing any repeat claim.
